description.narrative: The project development objective is to increase the provision of potable water to the residents in the project area within the Greater Beirut region, including those in the low-income neighborhoods of Southern Beirut, and to strengthen the capacity of the BeirutMount Lebanon Water Establishment in utility operations.

The project development objective of the Greater Beirut Water Supply Project for Lebanon is to increase the provision of potable water to the residents in the project area within the Greater Beirut region, including those in the low-income neighborhoods of Southern Beirut, and to strengthen the capacity of the Beirut Mount Lebanon Water Establishment in utility operations. There are three components to the project. Component one: bulk water supply infrastructure. Component one will comprise: (a) the construction and construction supervision of bulk water supply infrastructure; (b) design, construction and construction supervision of a water treatment plant (WTP) of 250,000 cubic meters a day capacity; (c) all related equipment including pumps and valves; and (d) support to Council for Development and Reconstruction for project management. Component two: supply reservoirs, distribution network and metering. Component two will comprise: (i) design, construction and construction supervision of 16 supply reservoirs of storage capacities varying between 500 and 1,000 m3 each, dispersed within the project area, and associated pumping stations; (ii) design, construction and construction supervision of water supply distribution network of about 187 km of pipelines across the project area in southern Beirut and parts of the Metn, Baabda and Aley areas; (iii) installation of 200,000 household meters in selected project areas; and (iv) installation of about 30 bulk water meters at reservoirs and distribution chambers. Component three: project management, utility strengthening and national studies. Component three will focus on utility strengthening and will also strengthen the capacity of the Ministry of Energy and Water for project oversight.

comment.narrative: Construction is ongoing but unlikely to be achieved. The WTP has been under construction since January 2019 and expected to be completed after the current closing date under the SGBWSP.

title.narrative: Volume (m3/day) of additional potable water distributed in the project area

comment.narrative: The remaining bulk infrastructure works not completed yet –the tunnel and pipelines remining works and the Water Treatment Plant. The target is not expected to be reached by the current closing date. The target corresponds to the designed treatment capacity of the Wardanieh WTP, and will be achieved once the whole system is operational. It corresponds to about 1.2 million people living in the Greater Beirut Area.

Unlikely to be achieved. There is a financing gap to cover the construction of the three reservoirs. The land for one of the three reservoirs has been fully expropriated. BMLWE has evaluated technical solutions to operate the system with different numbers of reservoirs. The Bulk reservoirs will be completed under the new SGBWSP.

title.narrative: TA for Design and operation of distribution system for 24/7 supply

comment.narrative: Achieved. The Beirut Mount Lebanon Water Establishment (BMLWE) completed the pilot in 2016 and installed smart-meters in the area. The BMLWE did not change the water tariff. Households are still paying a flat fee. BMLWE monitors the volume of water used and have noticed a reduction in the use of water as a result of the installation of the smart-meters.

title.narrative: Number of customers in Greater Beirut Mount Lebanon receiving 24/7 water supply

comment.narrative: Achieved, but not maintained. This indicator was achieved in 2018, and corresponds to the area in Achrafieh where 20,000 customer meters had been installed and where DMAs had been established. Before the Project in 2015, people in the pilot area had an intermittent supply (10 hours each 48 hours) of about 50000 m3 per day; during summer, only 30000 m3 per day (about 6 hours supply each 48 hours). Thanks to the Project activities (rehabilitation of network, installation of meter, creation of DMAs, NRW monitoring, etc) in 2018, the pilot area managed to receive continuous water supply of 24/7, at an average 42000 m3 per day. Unfortunately, since 2019 and the onset of several crises shaking the country, BMLWE has been unable to maintain this level of service. Still, 20,000 customers, corresponding to 84,000 beneficiaries are connected to a rehabilitated network that should be able to supply 24/7 supply if power supply is assured to pump enough water in the system. It is to be noted that the total number of customers that switched to 24/7 service in the zones under the Greater Beirut Water Supply Project (GBWSP) is estimated at 30,000 covering additional 10,000 people within the project area.
Partially achieved. 24 km of 2.8 diameter tunnels have been fully excavated in three stretches. The tunnels still need to be lined. Procurement to complete the tunnel lining works is ongoing.

title.narrative: New piped household connections for poor households in Southern Beirut that are resulting from the Project's intervention (cumulative) (Number)

comment.narrative: Partially Achieved. The household connections were completed for 5,125 household connections. The original target of 20,000 was a rough estimate done during preparation. However, as works progressed it became evident that the actual number of poor households connections in the area was lower. The actual number is 5,125 households, which have now been connected to BMLWE’s network. This corresponds to 21,525 beneficiaries.

Unlikely to be achieved and works stopped. The remaining works for the pipelines would be completed under the new loan SGBWSP (4km). 6 Km out of total 10 km had been completed in 2019 prior the bankruptcy of the main contractor. The contract has a physical progress of 52%

Achieved. Works completed. The works are completed with 432 km in the four zones. This indicator was overachieved with co-financing from the BMLWE. It corresponds to the rehabilitaion of all pipes installed prior to 1970, as well as new constructed areas were included. New household connections are 11,600.  ???????
